topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra
target_audience: Undergraduate students in Mathematics or Engineering

outline.topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in Mathematics or Engineering

sections.title: Prerequisite & Intuition: The 'Language' of Coordinates
sections.content: Define a basis as a coordinate system (a set of grid lines). Visualize the standard basis (x, y) as a square grid. Explain that a point (3, 2) is just a set of instructions: '3 steps along the red vector, 2 steps along the blue vector'.
sections.example: Imagine a character 'Pixel' living on a standard grid. The basis vectors {i, j} are his compass directions North and East.

sections.title: The Problem: Changing Perspectives
sections.content: Introduce a new 'tilted' basis. Show how the same point in space now needs different numbers to be described. Emphasize that the point hasn't moved, but our perspective has shifted.
sections.example: Pixel wears 'Magic Goggles' that tilt his world by 45 degrees. To him, the same stationary tree now looks like it's at different coordinate values.

sections.title: The Mechanism: The Transition Matrix (P)
sections.content: Formally derive the transition matrix P, where columns are the new basis vectors expressed in terms of the old basis. Equation: [v]_old = P * [v]_new. Use animation to show the mapping process.
sections.example: If the new basis vectors are {1,1} and {-1,1}, demonstrate how to build matrix P = [[1, -1], [1, 1]] to transform old coordinates to new ones.

sections.title: Application: Why Do We Care?
sections.content: Explain that we choose bases to make calculations easier (e.g., diagonalization). Use a visual of a complex shape that looks complicated in standard basis but becomes a simple rectangle in a 'smarter' basis.
sections.example: A robot arm (the device) calculating joint angles. It’s easier to describe the 'hand' position relative to the 'shoulder' (local basis) rather than the 'room' origin (global basis).

sections.title: Summary & Reflection
sections.content: Recap: (1) Basis = coordinate system, (2) Transition Matrix = translator between systems. Remind students: The space is invariant; only the description changes.
sections.example: Final shot: A map of a park. The map stays the same, but you can describe a treasure’s location starting from the 'Front Gate' or the 'Old Oak Tree'. Both are correct; one might just be easier for the treasure hunter.

lecture_lines: A basis acts as your coordinate system's grid. [Asset: grid_01]
Standard vectors i and j define your directions. [Asset: vectors_01]
Point (3, 2) is a simple set of instructions. [Asset: point_01]
animations: Display a coordinate grid centered at (0,0) in #FFFFFF.

Draw dashed lines from P to axes in #FFFF00.
Fade out the dashed lines and reset the grid.

storyboard.title: The Problem: Changing Perspectives
lecture_lines: Now introduce a new, tilted basis system. [Asset: tilt_01]
The point remains stationary in space. [Asset: static_point_01]
Coordinates change to describe the same location. [Asset: new_coords_01]
animations: Display two different basis sets, B1 and B2, in #FFFFFF.
Draw vector v represented in B1 basis in #00FFFF.
Show v transforming/rotating into B2 basis in #FF00FF.

storyboard.title: The Mechanism: The Transition Matrix (P)
lecture_lines: Transition matrix P translates between different bases. [Asset: matrix_p_01]
Columns of P are new basis vectors. [Asset: columns_01]
Visualize the mapping process between two grids. [Asset: mapping_01]
animations: Animate columns of P as basis vectors of B2 in #00FF00.
Multiply P by coordinates of v in B2 to get B1.

storyboard.title: Application: Why Do We Care?
lecture_lines: Choose bases to simplify complex mathematical calculations. [Asset: simplify_01]
Diagonalization makes shapes appear as simple rectangles. [Asset: rectangle_01]
Robots use local bases for easier control. [Asset: robot_01]
animations: Display a complex system, e.g., a rotating object.
Show how changing basis simplifies the representation.

storyboard.title: Summary & Reflection
lecture_lines: Basis is just a coordinate system choice. [Asset: recap_01]
Transition matrices act as system translators. [Asset: translator_01]
Perspective changes, but the space remains invariant. [Asset: invariant_01]
